root_idea.summary: The root centers on inclination or turning toward something, including approach, attachment, and adjacency.
root_idea.development: From inclination developed the senses of approaching or alighting as a guest, making something lean toward another, and being joined or situated at a side. Related extensions include enclosure, refuge, and hospitality.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic Form II verb is a distinct hospitality construction.
The Quranic nominal is the lexical item ضَيْف, guest or guests.

senses.definition: To receive, lodge, or entertain someone as a guest; to offer hospitality.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive hospitality construction, with the person received or entertained as its object.

senses.definition: A guest or guests; one who is received or lodged by another.
senses.usage_conditions: Because the noun originated as a verbal noun, it can refer to one guest or a group of guests, and to either sex.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incline toward or approach; of the sun, to incline toward setting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The approach sense may be used of a person, thing, or the sun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a woman, to menstruate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported lexical usage explained metaphorically as a transition away from purity; this interpretation is disputed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn aside from something; of an arrow, to miss or turn away from the target.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may take عَنْ with the thing from which one turns away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fear or be cautious of an event or affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension associated with being encompassed or beset by what one fears.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To alight at someone's abode as a guest, become his guest, or seek entertainment from him as a guest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The guest may be the subject who comes to another's dwelling; the same form can express seeking guest entertainment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of anxiety, to befall or descend upon someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use in which anxiety is treated as approaching or alighting upon its sufferer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To protect or defend someone, making him safe or free from fear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form II usage, distinct from receiving someone as a guest.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To straiten or distress someone; of anxiety, to befall him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical explanation is reported tentatively in the source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Possibly, to become someone's guest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An alternative, explicitly uncertain interpretation of the Form III entry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be reciprocal or correlative with something else.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of relations in which one term or entity is understood in connection with another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To run, hasten, or flee; of a dog, to run away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported lexical usage of the Form IV verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To look upon something from above, or to be on its brink, verge, or point.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The prepositional construction عَلَى الشَّيْءِ is part of this usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, to hear the stallion's voice with desire to go to him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage describing a she-camel's responsive inclination toward the stallion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Reciprocal or correlative relation; in particular, the relation of terms whose existence implies one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Examples include fathership and sonship, or other correlative nouns.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make something lean, rest, or stay against another thing; figuratively, to place an affair in someone's charge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction expresses physical support or the entrusting of a matter to someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to have recourse to something or to take refuge in it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the causative refuge sense of the Form IV construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To adjoin one thing to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general joining or attachment use, distinct from the grammatical technical term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In comparison with, or in relation to, something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional prepositional phrase meaning literally 'by addition to' or 'in juxtaposition to'.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone a guest, lodge him, give him refuge or asylum, and entertain him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive hospitality usage of the Form IV verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be collected together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported lexical noun-form usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be a follower or one who follows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized reported usage, distinct from merely approaching as a guest.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a valley, to become narrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form VI usage related to the notion of sides or constriction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come from both sides, surround, or hem someone or something in.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of people, beasts, dogs, or other parties approaching from the sides.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become joined, adjoined, or added to something; to join oneself to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source characterizes this usage as possibly postclassical.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask someone to grant protection or refuge; to have recourse to someone for protection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form X construction may express either requesting protection or taking refuge.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A menstruating woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare and disputed usage of the feminine noun, reported by one authority in connection with a poetic citation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A side or flank, especially the side of a valley or mountain; by extension, the vicinity or quarter of someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural ضِيفَانِ can refer to the two sides of a valley or another location.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who comes along with a guest, especially an uninvited intruder or follower of a guest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is ضَيَافِنُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hospitality or the act of entertaining guests; also a meal, banquet, or feast provided for them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun and substantive noun for receiving and entertaining guests.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person alighting as a guest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participle closely associated with the guest-arrival sense of ضَافَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An adjunct or adherent attached to a people or group without actually belonging to them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative passive-participial usage describing attachment without membership.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One whose origin or lineage is suspected, or who claims a relationship he does not possess.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may also describe someone whose origin is attributed to a group of which he is not a member.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One constrained to take refuge, especially someone in fear or burdened by distress.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sense includes a person driven to a confined place of refuge and calling for protection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One beset, hemmed in, or surrounded in war or battle; a person lacking strength among combatants.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized military and figurative usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One beset by distress of mind or constrained to seek refuge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is attested in poetic language for a person calling for aid.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Turning aside or crooked.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal or variant form; the source also reports it as a reading or equivalent of ضَائِفٌ in a poetic context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fleeing or turning away and fleeing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participle associated with the corresponding Form IV verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hardship, difficulty, or distress.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine noun usage distinct from the grammatical term الإضافة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place for receiving or entertaining guests.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place noun; its plural is مَضَايِفُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The master of an abode in which guests are entertained.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A person associated with the management or hosting of a guest-house or lodging place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who frequently entertains guests.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive nominal form describing habitual hospitality.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One asking or calling for aid or succour.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The active participle of the Form X refuge-seeking usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Anxiety, grief, want, or an affair that is feared or guarded against.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare and variant feminine form with several reported lexical explanations.

cautions: The reported menstruation senses of ضَافَ and ضَيْفَةٌ are disputed; the Quran-focused lexical discussion rejects that derivation, so they are retained only as broader reported Classical usages.
The Form III entry ضَايَفَهُ gives straitening as an apparent meaning but also tentatively suggests becoming a guest; both alternatives are marked as reported rather than certain.
The Form VII usage اِنْضَافَ إِلَيْهِ is explicitly described as possibly postclassical.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The Form III alternatives in lane-unit:Dyf:18188:g1:main cannot be resolved from the packet: straitening is reported alongside the possibility of becoming a guest, so both are preserved with conditional usage notes.
The variant report for مَضِيفٌ in lane-unit:Dyf:18201:g1:main is retained as a dialectal or textual alternative rather than treated as an unqualified standard headword.
